channel.title: AI Stupa Translation Project
channel.description: New English translations of texts from the Tibetan Buddhist canon, made by the AI Stupa (provisional, public domain).

item.title: The Noble Great Vehicle Sūtra on the Descent into Laṅkā (Toh 107)
item.description: The Noble Great Vehicle Sūtra on the Descent into Laṅkā, known in Sanskrit as the Āryalaṅkāvatāra Mahāyāna Sūtra and in Tibetan as Phakpa Langkar Shekpé Tekpa Chenpo'i Do, is one of the most influential scriptures of Mahāyāna Buddhism. It opens with the Buddha dwelling in the city of Laṅkā on the jewel-adorned summit of Mount Malaya by the ocean, surrounded by a great assembly of monks and of…

item.title: The Sevenfold Praise of the Glorious Guru Vanaratna (Toh 1177)
item.description: The Sevenfold Praise of the Glorious Guru Vanaratna, known in Sanskrit as Śrī Guru Vanaratna Stotra Saptaka and in Tibetan as Palden Lama Nakkyi Rinchen gyi Töpa Dünpa, is a short verse eulogy of the Indian monk and scholar Vanaratna, who was active in Nepal and Tibet in the fifteenth century. Its stanzas extol him as a strict keeper of the monastic vows of the Vinaya, a master of the Great…

item.title: In Praise of the Birth Stories (Toh 1178)
item.description: In Praise of the Birth Stories, known in Sanskrit as the Jātakastava and in Tibetan as Kyepa Rab kyi Töpa, is a devotional hymn in verse addressed to the Buddha. It celebrates the perfect conduct he showed in his former lives as a bodhisattva, recalling one birth story (jātaka) after another: the gift of his children and wife, the hare who offered his own body in the fire, the patience he kept…

item.title: In Praise of Gaṇeśvara (Toh 1175)
item.description: In Praise of Gaṇeśvara, known in Sanskrit as the Gaṇeśvarastava and in Tibetan as Tsokkyi Wangchuk gi Töpa, is a short hymn in eight verses to Gaṇeśvara, the elephant-faced "Lord of the Hosts," better known as Gaṇeśa or Gaṇapati, who in Buddhist tantric practice is honored as a lord of obstacles and a giver of wealth and accomplishment. Its verses praise his tusked elephant face, his jeweled body…

item.title: The Jewel of Praise for Glorious Śabarapāda (Toh 1176)
item.description: The Jewel of Praise for Glorious Śabarapāda, in Sanskrit Śrīśabarapādastotra and in Tibetan Dpal ri khrod zhabs kyi bstod pa rin po che, is a tantric hymn in verse honoring Śabara, the great Indian mahāsiddha who lived as a hunter-yogin in the mountains. It opens by explaining his name syllable by syllable and then praises him as a guru and lord of yogins, taking each part of his attire in turn…

item.title: In Praise of the Holy Guru, the Dharma King (Toh 1172)
item.description: In Praise of the Holy Guru, the Dharma King, whose Sanskrit title is given as Paramanagurudharmārājastotra and whose Tibetan title is Lama Dampa Chökyi Gyalpo la Töpa, is a short hymn of four ornate verses composed by the Indian paṇḍita and great poet Lakṣmīkara, who translated it into Tibetan together with the translator Shongtön at the temple of glorious Sakya. The master it celebrates is not…

item.title: In Praise of the Venerable Lokeśvara Siṃhanāda (Toh 1173)
item.description: In Praise of the Venerable Lokeśvara Siṃhanāda, known in Sanskrit as the Siṃhanādalokeśvarabhaṭṭārakastuti and in Tibetan as Jetsün Jikten Wangchuk Sengé Dra la Töpa, is a hymn in ornate verse to Siṃhanāda, the "Lion's Roar," a form of Avalokiteśvara, the bodhisattva of compassion, who is especially invoked as a healer of disease. Its verses praise his love for beings, his lion mount, his trident…

item.title: The Jewel Garland Praise of Lokeśvara (Toh 1174)
item.description: The Jewel Garland Praise of Lokeśvara, in Sanskrit Lokeśvararatnamālāstava and in Tibetan Jikten Wangchuk gi Töpa Rinpoché Trengwa, is a hymn in verse to Lokeśvara, the bodhisattva of compassion better known as Avalokiteśvara. It praises him as one who, though single, appears in many forms to those he trains, like the moon reflected in many vessels of water. In the manner of the Kāraṇḍavyūha…

item.title: The Noble Dharma Discourse Called "The Eight Maṇḍalas," a Great Vehicle Sūtra (Toh 105)
item.description: The Noble Dharma Discourse Called "The Eight Maṇḍalas," a Great Vehicle Sūtra, is known in Sanskrit as the Ārya Maṇḍala Aṣṭa Nāma Mahāyāna Sūtra and in Tibetan as Phakpa Kyilkhor Gyé Chejawé Chökyi Namdrang Thekpa Chenpoi Do. It is a Mahāyāna sūtra set at Śrāvastī, in the Jeta Grove of Anāthapiṇḍada's park, where the Buddha is teaching before a vast assembly of monks, bodhisattvas, gods, and…

item.title: The Glorious Great Marvel Illuminating the Profound Meaning (Toh 1200)
item.description: The Glorious Great Marvel Illuminating the Profound Meaning, in Sanskrit Śrī Guhyārthaprakāśa Mahādbhuta and in Tibetan Pal Zabmö Dön Salwa Mé Du Jungwa Chenpo, is a commentary on the Mahāmudrātilaka, a tantra of the unsurpassed yoga class. Opening with homage to Vajrasattva and to the protector whose very self is the Great Seal, it sets out, chapter by chapter, the meaning of that tantra as the…

item.title: The Jewel Garland: A Commentary on the Difficult Points of the Tantra of the Glorious Lamp of Reality (Toh 1205)
item.description: The Jewel Garland, in full A Commentary on the Difficult Points of the Tantra of the Glorious Lamp of Reality, carries the Sanskrit title Śrī Tattvapradīpaṃ Nāma Tantra Ratnamālā Pañcikā and the Tibetan title Pal De Khona Nyi kyi Drönmé Gyü kyi Kadrel Rinchen Trengwa. It is a commentary on the difficult points of a tantra, the Glorious Lamp of Reality: after paying homage to Glorious Great Bliss…

item.title: Commentary on the Intentional Language (Toh 1206)
item.description: The Commentary on the Intentional Language, whose Sanskrit title is transcribed in the Tibetan as Samādhibhāṣaṭīka and whose Tibetan title is Gongpé Ké kyi Drelpa, is Toh 1206 in the Tengyur, where it belongs among the commentaries on the tantras. It explains the intentional or coded language of the tantras, the secret vocabulary in which words such as liquor and strength, along with obscure…

item.title: The Noble Great Vehicle Sūtra "The Blessing of All the Tathāgatas, Watching over Sentient Beings and Fully Displaying the Arrangement of the Buddhafields" (Toh 98)
item.description: The Blessing of All the Tathāgatas, Watching over Sentient Beings and Fully Displaying the Arrangement of the Buddhafields is a Great Vehicle sūtra whose Sanskrit title is given as Ārya Sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānasattvāvalokanabuddhakṣetranirdeśanavyūha, and whose Tibetan title begins Phakpa Dezhin Shekpa Tamché kyi Jingyi Lap Semchen la Zik shing Sangyé kyi Zhing gi. The discourse opens on Mount…

item.title: The Sūtra of the Eight Lights, the Clear and Vast Dharma of the Buddha (Toh 1067)
item.description: The Sūtra of the Eight Lights, whose full title is The Sūtra Called the Eight Lights, the Clear and Vast Dharma of the Buddha, and whose Tibetan title is Sangyé kyi Chö Selzhing Yangpa Nanggyé, is Toh 1067 in the Kangyur, where it is placed in the collection of dhāraṇī texts; it gives no Sanskrit title, since it derives from a scripture composed in Chinese, the Sūtra of the Eight Yang of Heaven…

item.title: The Noble Aspiration Prayer of Maitreya (Toh 1096)
item.description: The Noble Aspiration Prayer of Maitreya, in Tibetan Phakpa Jampé Mönlam, is Toh 1096 in the Kangyur, where it is placed in the dhāraṇī collection among the canon's aspiration prayers; the Tibetan text gives no Sanskrit title. It is a short prayer in verse that follows the classic sequence of Mahāyāna devotion: homage to the buddhas, bodhisattvas, and śrāvakas and to the mind of awakening…

item.title: Verses of Benediction (Toh 1107)
item.description: The Verses of Benediction, in Tibetan Shipar Jöpé Tsiksu Chépa, is a short collection of auspicious verses that, as its closing lines state, is drawn from the chapter on the merchants Trapuṣa and Bhallika in the noble Lalitavistara Sūtra, the account of the Buddha's life known in English as The Play in Full. In that chapter the two merchants offer food to the newly awakened Buddha, and these…

item.title: The Noble Great Vehicle Sūtra "The Questions of the Divine Son Susthitamati" (Toh 80)
item.description: The Noble Great Vehicle Sūtra called The Questions of the Divine Son Susthitamati, known in Sanskrit as the Āryasusthitamatidevaputraparipṛcchā and in Tibetan as Phags pa lha'i bu blo gros rab gnas kyis zhus pa, is a Mahāyāna discourse set on Vulture Peak near Rājagṛha, where the Buddha is joined by a vast assembly of renowned arhats and bodhisattvas, among them Mañjuśrī, Maitreya, and…

item.title: The Recitation of the Names of the Tathāgatas: A Garland of Ornaments of the Fortunate Eon (Toh 1169)
item.description: The Recitation of the Names of the Tathāgatas: A Garland of Ornaments of the Fortunate Eon, in Sanskrit Tathāgatanāmasaṅgītikālpikabhadrālaṃkaramāla and in Tibetan De bzhin gshegs pa'i mtshan brjod bskal bzang rgyan gyi phreng ba, is a devotional work in verse honoring the thousand buddhas who appear in our present world age, the Fortunate Eon. It opens by recalling how, in a distant eon, the…

item.title: Praise to the Deities of the Four Yogas (Toh 1170)
item.description: The Praise to the Deities of the Four Yogas, in Sanskrit Yogacaturadevastotra and in Tibetan Jorwa Zhi Lha la Töpa, is a devotional hymn in verse that opens with homage to the Blessed Mother, the Perfection of Wisdom. It first praises the Buddha as he appears at the opening of the large Perfection of Wisdom sūtras, seated in the samādhi called the King of Samādhis and filling the worlds of the…

item.title: In Praise of the Great Scholar Drakpa Gyaltsen (Toh 1171)
item.description: In Praise of the Great Scholar Drakpa Gyaltsen, whose Sanskrit title is given as Mahāpaṇḍitakīrtijastotra and whose Tibetan title is Khepa Chenpo Drakpa Gyaltsen la Töpa, is a short devotional poem honoring Drakpa Gyaltsen, who lived from 1147 to 1216 and was one of the great founding masters of the Sakya tradition of Tibet. It was composed by the Indian preceptor Sugataśrī, who translated it…

item.title: The Noble Great Vehicle Sūtra called The Questions of the Householder Ugra (Toh 63)
item.description: The Noble Great Vehicle Sūtra called The Questions of the Householder Ugra, known in Sanskrit as the Āryagṛhapati Ugraparipṛcchā Nāma Mahāyānasūtra and in Tibetan as Phakpa Khyimdak Drakshulchen Gyi Zhupa, is a Mahāyāna sūtra in which the Buddha, staying at Śrāvastī in Prince Jeta's Grove with a great assembly of monks and bodhisattvas such as Maitreya, Mañjuśrī, and Avalokiteśvara, responds to…

item.title: Praise of the Eight Tathāgatas (Toh 1166)
item.description: Praise of the Eight Tathāgatas, known in Sanskrit as Aṣṭa Tathāgata Stotra and in Tibetan as Dezhin Shekpa Gyé la Töpa, is a devotional hymn in verse to the eight buddhas of the Medicine Buddha tradition, and its closing line attributes its composition to the master Śāntarakṣita. It praises each buddha in turn, from the King of Marks, Svaraghoṣarāja, Suvarṇabhadravimala, Aśokottamaśrī…

item.title: The Praise of the Earliest Dawn (Toh 1167)
item.description: The Praise of the Earliest Dawn, known in Sanskrit as the Suprabhātastotra and in Tibetan as Rabtu Ngawar Namlangpé Töpa, is a hymn in verse to the Buddha, which its colophon ascribes to Śrī Harṣadeva, king of Kashmir. In the manner of an Indian dawn hymn, it pictures one by one the great gods and sages of the Indian world, Brahmā, Śiva with Pārvatī, Indra, Viṣṇu, Agni, Balarāma, Gaṇeśa, and…

item.title: Praise in Homage to the Stūpas of the Eight Great Places (Toh 1168)
item.description: Praise in Homage to the Stūpas of the Eight Great Places, known in Sanskrit as Aṣṭamahāsthānacaityavandanāstava and in Tibetan as Né Chenpo Gyé kyi Chöten la Chaktsalwé Töpa, is a short devotional hymn in verse which, according to its colophon, was composed by Śrī Harṣadeva, king of Kashmir, for the sake of his mother. It pays homage to the stūpas marking the great events of the Buddha's life…

item.title: Extensive Commentary on The Song of Glorious Vajradhara, a Praise of the Blessed One (Toh 1163)
item.description: The Extensive Commentary on The Song of Glorious Vajradhara, a Praise of the Blessed One, known in Sanskrit as the Śrī Vajradhara Saṃgīta Bhagavati Stotra Ṭīkā and in Tibetan as Chomdendé la Töpa Pal Dorjé Dzin gyi Yang kyi Gyacher Shepa, is Toh 1163 in the Tengyur, where it belongs to the section of praises (stotra). It is a close commentary on a short hymn to the buddhas, which it reads as both…

item.title: Praise of the Five Tathāgatas (Toh 1164)
item.description: Praise of the Five Tathāgatas, known in Sanskrit as Pañca Tathāgata Stava and in Tibetan as Dezhin Shekpa Nga la Töpa, is a short hymn in verse addressed to the five buddhas of tantric Buddhism. After an opening homage to the Lord of Speech, it devotes a stanza to each buddha in turn, Vairocana, Akṣobhya, Ratnasambhava, Amitābha and Amoghasiddhi, describing the color of his body, his radiance…

item.title: The Praise of the Seven Tathāgatas (Toh 1165)
item.description: The Praise of the Seven Tathāgatas, known in Sanskrit as the Saptatathāgatastotra and in Tibetan as Dezhin Shekpa Dün gyi Töpa, is a short hymn in verse honoring the seven buddhas of the past. Opening with homage to the youthful Mañjuśrī, it gives one verse of praise to each of the seven in turn, Vipaśyin, Śikhin, Viśvabhū, Krakucchanda, Kanakamuni, Kāśyapa, and Śākyamuni, celebrating their…

item.title: The Noble Great Vehicle Sūtra called The Meeting of the Father and the Son (Toh 60)
item.description: The Meeting of the Father and the Son, known in Sanskrit as the Pitāputrasamāgamana Sūtra and in Tibetan as Yab dang sras mjal ba, is a Great Vehicle sūtra that also bears the subtitle "the Definitive Teaching on Reality." It recounts the Buddha's meeting with his father, King Śuddhodana, along with members of the Śākya clan, an occasion on which the Buddha teaches the ultimate nature of things…

item.title: Commentary on the Praise of Confession (Toh 1160)
item.description: The Commentary on the Praise of Confession, in Sanskrit Deśanāstavavṛtti and in Tibetan Bshags pa'i bstod pa'i 'grel pa, is an Indian commentary on a short hymn in which the poet confesses his misdeeds before the Buddha while praising him as the unequaled king of physicians, a hymn whose author the commentary identifies by the name Candra, traditionally Candragomin. Working through the hymn line…

item.title: The Praise Called the Empowerment of the Buddha (Toh 1161)
item.description: The Praise Called the Empowerment of the Buddha, whose Sanskrit title is given as Śuddhābhiṣekanāmastotra and which is known in Tibetan as Sangyé Wangkurwa Zhejawé Töpa, is a short hymn in verse celebrating the birth of the Buddha Śākyamuni. It tells how the Sage, having perfected the perfections over three countless eons, came down from the heavens to be conceived in the womb of Queen Māyādevī…

item.title: Praise of the Blessed One, the Song of Glorious Vajradhara (Toh 1162)
item.description: Praise of the Blessed One, the Song of Glorious Vajradhara, known in Sanskrit as Śrī Vajradhara Saṃgīti Bhagavān Stotraḥ and in Tibetan as Chomden Dé la Töpa Pal Dorjé Dzin gyi Yang, is a short devotional hymn in verse. Opening with homage to glorious Vajrasattva and bearing the name of Vajradhara, the tantric form of the Buddha, it belongs to the tantric strand of Buddhist devotional poetry. Its…

item.title: The Rite of the Single-Syllable Mantra of Noble Mañjuśrī (Toh 896)
item.description: The Rite of the Single-Syllable Mantra of Noble Mañjuśrī, known in Tibetan as 'Phags pa 'jam dpal gyi sngags yi ge 'bru gcig pa'i cho ga, is a brief ritual text centered on a one-syllable mantra of Mañjuśrī, the bodhisattva of wisdom. It opens by praising the mantra as supremely secret, as the heart essence of all the Tathāgatas, and as able to accomplish every aim and fulfill every hope. It then…

item.title: The Dhāraṇī Called the Vast (Toh 897)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī Called the Vast, Perfect, Unobstructed Mind of Great Compassion of the Noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, Who Has a Thousand Hands and a Thousand Eyes, known in Tibetan as Phakpa Changchub Sempa Chenrezik Wangchuk Chaktong Chentong Dang Denpa, is a dhāraṇī scripture centered on the thousand-armed, thousand-eyed form of Avalokiteśvara, the bodhisattva who embodies the compassion of all…

item.title: The Dhāraṇī Called the Essence of the Unobstructed Wish-Fulfilling Wheel (Toh 898)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī Called the Essence of the Unobstructed Wish-Fulfilling Wheel, the Secret Treasury of the Noble Avalokiteśvara is known in Tibetan by a title beginning Phakpa Chenrezik Wangchuk gi Sangwé Dzö Tokpa Mepé Yishin, and it belongs to the textual tradition centered on Avalokiteśvara's wish-fulfilling wheel. It is a dhāraṇī text, a scripture centered on a sacred incantation. It opens on the…

item.title: The Dhāraṇī of the Noble Eleven-Faced Avalokiteśvara (Toh 899)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī of the Noble Eleven-Faced Avalokiteśvara, known in Sanskrit as the Ārya Avalokiteśvara Ekādaśamukha Nāma Dhāraṇī and in Tibetan by a title beginning Phakpa Chenrezik, is a short scripture centered on the powerful heart mantra of Avalokiteśvara in his eleven-faced form. In it, the bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara comes before the Buddha, accompanied by many holders of mantras, and explains…

item.title: The Hundred and Eight Names of Noble Avalokiteśvara (Toh 900)
item.description: The Hundred and Eight Names of Noble Avalokiteśvara, known in Sanskrit as the Āryāvalokiteśvarasya Nāmāṣṭaśataka and in Tibetan as the Phakpa Chenrezik Wangchuk gi Tsen Gya Tsa Gyepa, is a short scripture praising the bodhisattva of compassion through a litany of one hundred and eight names and epithets. It opens in the manner of a sutra, with the Blessed One dwelling at Avalokiteśvara's own…

item.title: The Noble Great Vehicle Sūtra Called the Heart of Amoghapāśa (Toh 901)
item.description: The Noble Great Vehicle Sūtra Called the Heart of Amoghapāśa, known in Sanskrit as the Āryāmoghapāśahṛdayanāmamahāyānasūtra and in Tibetan as Phakpa Dönyö Zhakpé Nyingpo, is a Mahāyāna scripture centered on Amoghapāśa, the form of the bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara whose name means "Unfailing Lasso," symbolizing his ability to draw beings to liberation. The discourse is set on the summit of Mount…

item.title: The Noble Great Vehicle Sūtra called The Array of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya (Toh 50)
item.description: The Array of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, known in Sanskrit as the Akṣobhyatathāgatasya Vyūha and in Tibetan as De bzhin gshegs pa mi 'khrugs pa'i bkod pa, is a Great Vehicle sūtra presented as the sixth chapter of the Heap of Jewels collection. It opens with the Buddha staying on Vulture Peak Mountain near Rājagṛha, accompanied by a great assembly of twelve hundred and fifty monks, all of them…

item.title: The Spell Taught by Mañjuśrī (Toh 893)
item.description: Toh 893 in the Kangyur is a short spell text centered on the bodhisattva Mañjuśrī. Its full English, Sanskrit, and Tibetan titles cannot be confirmed from the opening lines alone. After homage to the Three Jewels and to the Gentle Protector, Mañjuśrī in his youthful form rises before the Blessed One and the assembled gathering and offers to reveal a supreme spell, or vidyā, which he says will be…

item.title: The Names of Noble Mañjuśrī (Toh 894)
item.description: The Names of Noble Mañjuśrī is a very brief dhāraṇī-style text devoted to the bodhisattva of wisdom, Mañjuśrī. Its Tibetan title is likely along the lines of Phakpa Jampal gyi Tsen, and a Sanskrit form is not clearly attested in the source lines. After an opening homage to noble Mañjuśrī, it gives a short series of mantric names, each introduced by the syllables oṃ bākye. It then declares that…

item.title: The Dhāraṇī of the Venerable Noble Mañjuśrī Called "Increasing Wisdom and Intelligence" (Toh 895)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī of the Venerable Noble Mañjuśrī Called "Increasing Wisdom and Intelligence," known in Sanskrit as Ārya Mañjuśrī Bhaṭṭārakasya Prajñā Buddhi Vardhana Nāma Dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Rje btsun 'phags pa 'jam dpal gyi shes rab dang blo 'phel ba zhes bya ba'i gzungs, is a brief incantation devoted to the bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, the embodiment of wisdom. After an homage to the Three Jewels…

item.title: The Incantation for Remembering Past Births (Toh 889)
item.description: The Heart of Sukhāvatī, known in Tibetan as Dewachen gyi Nyingpo and likely corresponding to a Sanskrit title such as Sukhāvatīhṛdaya, is a brief incantation text, or dhāraṇī, centered on the noble bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara. It opens with homage to the Buddha, the Dharma, the Saṅgha, and Avalokiteśvara, then presents a short mantra that the reciter asks to be accomplished on their behalf. It…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "The Vow of Maitreya" (Toh 890)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "The Vow of Maitreya," known in Sanskrit as Ārya Maitrī Pratijñā Nāma Dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Phakpa Jampé Dam Chepa Zhejawé Zung, is a short incantatory text devoted to Maitreya, the bodhisattva who is destined to become the next buddha of our world. After paying homage to the Three Jewels and to Maitreya, it presents a sequence of three mantras, a root secret mantra…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "Spoken by Mañjuśrī" (Toh 892)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī Called "Spoken by Noble Mañjuśrī," known in Sanskrit as the Ārya Mañjuśrī Svākhyāta Nāma Dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Phakpa Jampal gyi Zhal ne Sungpa zhe Jawé Zung, is a short incantation text devoted to the bodhisattva of wisdom. After paying homage to the Three Jewels and to Mañjuśrī, it presents a mantra that invokes the light of wisdom, asks for the protection of the vajra-like mind…

item.title: The Noble Mahāyāna Sūtra "The Display of Amitābha" (Toh 49)
item.description: The Noble Great Vehicle Sūtra called The Display of Amitābha, known in Sanskrit as the Ārya Amitābhavyūha Nāma Mahāyāna Sūtra and in Tibetan as Pakpa Ö Pakmé Kyi Köpa, is a Mahāyāna sūtra devoted to the buddha Amitābha and the splendor of his realm. It opens with the Buddha at Vulture Peak Mountain near Rājagṛha, surrounded by a great assembly of thirty-two thousand monks who are all arhats. It…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "Heap of Flowers" (Toh 886)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "Heap of Flowers," known in Sanskrit as the Āryapuṣpakūṭanāmadhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Pakpa Metok Tsekpa Zhejawé Zung, is a dhāraṇī text, a scripture centered on a sacred incantation believed to carry protective and spiritually transformative power. It opens with the Buddha dwelling at the great lake Anavatapta, in the palace of the nāga king of the same name. He is…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called Great Mahīndra (Toh 887)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called Great Mahīndra, known in Sanskrit as the Ārya Mahāmahīndra Nāma Dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Phakpa Sai Wangpo Chenpo Zhe Jawai Zung, is a short scripture centered on a dhāraṇī, a sacred formula of protective and spiritual power. It opens in the classic sūtra style, recounting that the buddha Samantaprabha was staying in the dwelling of the brahmin Mahāmahīndra, a place…

item.title: The Noble Great Dhāraṇī (Toh 888)
item.description: The Noble Great Dhāraṇī, known in Sanskrit as the Āryamahādhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Phagpa Zung Chenpo, is a short scripture centered on a protective incantation taught by the Buddha. It opens at Śrāvastī, in Prince Jeta's Grove, where the Blessed One is staying with a great assembly of twelve hundred and fifty monks. The venerable Ānanda, having completed the summer rains retreat in the city of…

item.title: The Introduction to the Birth Stories (Toh 32)
item.description: The Introduction to the Birth Stories, known in Sanskrit as the Jātakanidāna and in Tibetan as Kyepa Rab kyi Lengzhi, is a narrative work that sets the stage for the Buddha's tales of his former lives. It opens in the Jeta Grove at Anāthapiṇḍada's park, where the elder Arthadarśin asks the Blessed One to teach the lineage of the buddhas. The compilers then introduce the background of the birth…

item.title: The Sūtra of Great Auspiciousness (Toh 43)
item.description: The Sūtra of Great Auspiciousness, known in Sanskrit as the Mahāmaṅgala Sūtra and in Tibetan as the Bkra shis chen po'i mdo, is a short discourse in which the Buddha explains what truly constitutes auspiciousness. Its setting is the Jeta Grove at Śrāvastī, in the park of Anāthapiṇḍada. There, in the night, a host of gods illuminates the grove with many-colored light, approaches the Buddha, and…
